description_full: Bank7 Corp. operates as a bank holding company for Bank7 that provides banking and financial services to individual and corporate customers. It provides commercial deposit, commercial checking, money market, and other deposit accounts; and retail deposit services, such as certificates of deposit, money market accounts, checking accounts, negotiable order of withdrawal accounts, savings accounts, and automated teller machine access. The company also offers commercial real estate, hospitality, energy, and commercial and industrial lending services; and consumer lending services to individuals for personal and household purposes comprising residential real estate loans and mortgage banking services, personal lines of credit, loans for the purchase of automobiles, and other installment loans, as well as secured and unsecured term loans and home improvement loans. It operates through a network of full-service branches in Oklahoma, the Dallas/Fort Worth, Texas metropolitan area, and Kansas. The company was formerly known as Haines Financial Corp. Bank7 Corp. was founded in 1901 and is headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

financial_summary: Bank7 Corp. is a small-cap financial services business with a $628M market cap on $96M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 20% against a 8% cost of capital — a 11-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $41M in free cash flow — roughly 43 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.07× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 1.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 1.5%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 49% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
